## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: `--json` takes the next argument as its path even when that argument is another flag. As a result, `--json --junit out.xml` raises an error instead of writing both reports. This review traced `parse_args` and `write_reports` in `app/cli.py` and read both tests in `tests/test_cli.py`; it did not run them. The `--junit` validation correctly rejects a missing path and a following flag, and `test_required_junit_path` covers both cases.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `--json` option to `parse_args`. The option uses the given path, or `results.json` when no path is supplied. It also adds `write_reports`, which writes each parsed report kind to its destination, and new tests for both options.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — Stop `--json` from consuming a following flag as its path — With `["--json", "--junit", "out.xml"]`, `parse_args` sets the JSON destination to `"--junit"` and skips that flag. It then raises `ValueError("unknown option: out.xml")`. Lines 15–19 check only `i + 1 < len(args)` and never test `args[i + 1].startswith("--")`, which the `--junit` branch at line 7 does test. The comment at line 12, "JSON can use its default destination when no path is supplied", is also false for this input. No test passes `--json` followed by another flag. — Your PR body says `--json` works "alongside the required --junit destination", but putting `--json` before `--junit` fails with a misleading error about `out.xml`, and no report is written. — Fix: Use the default only when `i + 1 == len(args)` or `args[i + 1].startswith("--")`, as line 7 does. Otherwise consume the next argument. Add a test for `parse_args(["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"]) == {"json": "results.json", "junit": "x.xml"}`.
